note: Editorial handling notes written for this curriculum. These are judgements about classroom use, not claims about the sources -- all factual metadata lives in verified-sources.json and comes from the repositories.

loc-2005625331: The map's own 1679 title uses period French racial terminology. Show the title as it is and name it as evidence of how European mapmakers wrote about Africa; do not silently rewrite it.
loc-96687096: Latin title carries period racial terminology. Handle as above.
loc-98504459: The Library of Congress records this copy as published Liverpool, 1884 -- an abolitionist-era reprint of the 1788 stowage diagram, not the 1788 printing itself. Have the learner date the diagram and this copy separately.
Depicts the Middle Passage. Preview before use; pair with a named individual account rather than showing the diagram alone.
loc-44015764: First-person account of enslavement and the Middle Passage. Preview and select passages before assigning.
loc-2020637509: A commercial calendar print of an Ojibwe leader produced by a non-Native printing firm. Use it as an object of source critique -- who made this image, for what audience, and what does it leave out -- not as an Anishinaabe-authored source.
loc-2025887093: The treaty texts are primary; the 1904 volume is the federal government's own compilation of them. Have the learner name both layers when citing.
nara-jacksons-message-indian-removal: A removal-era executive argument. Read it as advocacy, and pair it with the treaty record rather than as neutral description.
nara-dred-scott: Contains the Court's reasoning denying Black citizenship. Preview; teach as a decision that was later overturned by the Reconstruction amendments in this same registry.
nara-plessy-v-ferguson: Upholds segregation. Preview; pair with the 14th Amendment entry.
nara-chinese-exclusion-act: Exclusionary immigration law. Preview and frame as a federal action to be evaluated, not endorsed.
nara-dawes-act: Allotment law that broke up tribal landholding. Pair with the treaty record.
met-551786: Funerary papyrus; includes religious imagery of the dead.
met-548344: Funerary papyrus; includes religious imagery of the dead.
loc-2008678196: An 1898 commercial photograph of a site built centuries earlier. The dwelling is the pre-contact evidence; the photograph is a much later record of it. Have the learner date both layers separately.
met-319871: Dates from 1830-60, after sustained contact. Present it as Great Lakes Indigenous work of its own period, not as evidence of pre-contact life.
avalon-hamcode: Avalon's page states the text is 'Translated by L. W. King'; the companion introduction page (ancient/hammint.asp) is credited to Charles F. Horne, 1915. The law code is the primary source; the English wording and the introduction are later layers, and the learner should cite both.
met-316442: Carved in West Africa around 1490-1530 for European buyers. It is African work and evidence of Atlantic trade at the same time -- ask the learner who made it, who commissioned it, and how they can tell.
met-450418: The Met records only country (Syria), date, and medium for this bowl; do not attribute a maker or a workshop it does not name.
